findings.title: Coordinate-space inconsistency between hit-testing and preview
findings.message: Edge detection uses `clip` (ContentBBox, scene-local) compared against e.Pos(). The test adds scene.SceneGeom.Pos to positions elsewhere, suggesting event positions are window-based while Geom boxes are scene-relative. `destination` and the edge logic use `p.In(clip)` with raw positions, so insertion and edge scrolling may be wrong for modal sheets whose scene origin is nonzero, while `preview` adds SceneGeom.Pos to the clip.
findings.suggestion: Convert e.Pos() to scene coordinates (subtract scene.SceneGeom.Pos) consistently before comparing with Geom values in destination and edge scrolling.

finding.title: Scope comparison may spuriously cancel or retain drags
finding.message: The early return compares scopes by pointer equality. If a tab scope is closed/revoked, the pointers are unchanged but visibility is computed false by the caller, which is covered by `visible`. However, the check ignores `r.control.a`/window changes, and `b.end()` on every real change cancels a live drag whenever any scope slice differs (for example, when a dialog scope is replaced). This is plausible, but the bigger risk is that publication happens during sync while a gesture is live.
finding.suggestion: Compare only fields that matter for revocation, and document that scope changes cancel the drag.
finding.evidence: old.input.visible == visible && old.input.disabled == r.control.disabled && slices.Equal(old.input.scopes, scopes)
